## Load packages

`pacman` loads the required packages and installs any that are missing. `here::i_am()` places
this notebook in the repository, so paths resolve from the repository root. `singscore` is called
with `::`.

```{r setup}
pacman::p_load(here, dplyr, tibble, purrr, stringr, ggplot2, patchwork, readxl, writexl)
here::i_am("03_Pathway_Enrichment/04_run_singscore/a_script/04_run_singscore.qmd")
```

## Read inputs

singscore gives each sample one score per gene set. Within a sample it ranks every gene by
abundance, then scores a set by how high its members rank on average, centred so that 0 is what
random members would give. The ranks are within the sample, so a score ignores the rest of the
cohort; there is no p-value and no contrast. Later steps (`05_set_classification`,
`06_set_association`) test the scores.

The inputs are the tested sets, the catalogue and protein-to-gene map from `00_build_gene_sets`,
and the protein abundance matrix from quantification.

```{r read}
stage <- here("03_Pathway_Enrichment", "04_run_singscore")
gene_sets <- here("03_Pathway_Enrichment", "00_build_gene_sets", "c_data")
sets <- readRDS(file.path(gene_sets, "gene_sets.rds"))
book <- file.path(gene_sets, "00_build_gene_sets.xlsx")
set_catalog <- read_excel(book, "set_catalog")
protein_map <- read_excel(book, "protein_gene_map")
proteins <- readRDS(here("01_Preprocess", "02_Quantification", "c_data", "proteins.rds"))
dim(proteins$E)
```

## Score samples

Sets are keyed on gene symbols, so the matrix keeps the representative protein of each symbol
and its rows are renamed from protein to gene. `rankGenes()` ranks genes within each sample;
`multiScore()` scores every set in every sample and returns `Scores`, a set-by-sample matrix,
beside `Dispersions`, the spread of each set's member ranks within each sample.

```{r score}
gene_map <- filter(protein_map, selected)
gene_matrix <- proteins$E[gene_map$protein, ]
rownames(gene_matrix) <- gene_map$gene
scored <- singscore::multiScore(singscore::rankGenes(gene_matrix), upSetColc = sets)
scores <- scored$Scores
dim(scores)
scores[1:4, 1:4]
```

## Score and dispersion per set

Dispersion is low when a set's members sit together in the ranking and high when they scatter.
Average each set's score and dispersion across samples, then summarise by collection.

```{r spread}
set_spread <- set_catalog |>
  filter(qualifies) |>
  select(set_id, database) |>
  mutate(
    score = rowMeans(scores[set_id, ]),
    dispersion = rowMeans(scored$Dispersions[set_id, ])
  )
collection_spread <- set_spread |>
  summarise(
    sets = n(), median_score = round(median(score), 4),
    median_dispersion = round(median(dispersion), 1), .by = database
  )
collection_spread
```

## Check participant structure

A principal component analysis of the scores (samples as rows) shows what drives them. For the
first two components, the R² of a linear model on participant gives the share of that
component's variance explained by participant identity. `proteins$targets` rows follow the matrix
columns, so they line up with the component scores.

```{r structure}
components <- prcomp(t(scores))
structure_check <- tibble(
  component = paste0("PC", 1:4),
  variance_explained = round(summary(components)$importance[2, 1:4], 3),
  participant_share = c(round(map_dbl(1:2, function(i) {
    summary(lm(components$x[, i] ~ proteins$targets$participant))$r.squared
  }), 3), NA, NA)
)
structure_check
```

Participant identity dominates the raw scores, so later steps use the within-leg change, never
the raw value.

## Figure

singscore's own `plotDispersion()` and `plotRankDensity()` draw one signature at a time. These
cohort-scale views are plain ggplots over the matrices `multiScore()` already returned: panel A
plots each set's mean score against mean dispersion, panel B every score pooled within study
group.

```{r figure}
group_scores <- tibble(
  group = rep(proteins$targets$group, each = nrow(scores)),
  score = as.vector(scores)
)
figure <- wrap_plots(
  ggplot(set_spread, aes(score, dispersion, colour = database)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3, colour = "grey80") +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.4, size = 0.8) +
    scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Dark2", name = NULL) +
    guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 3, alpha = 1))) +
    labs(
      x = "mean score across samples", y = "mean dispersion across samples",
      title = "Set score against dispersion"
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 10),
  ggplot(group_scores, aes(score, group)) +
    geom_violin(fill = "grey85", colour = NA) +
    geom_boxplot(width = 0.12, outlier.shape = NA, linewidth = 0.3) +
    labs(x = "singscore", y = NULL, title = "Score distribution by study group") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 10),
  ncol = 1, heights = c(1.4, 1)
) +
  plot_annotation(
    caption = str_wrap(paste(
      "S11 Figure. singscore across the cohort.",
      sprintf("(A) One point per set, %d sets, score and dispersion averaged", nrow(scores)),
      sprintf("over %d samples.", ncol(scores)),
      "Dispersion is the spread of a set's member ranks within a sample: low means members sit",
      "together. (B) Every set in every sample, pooled within study group; the box is the",
      "interquartile range. Data: set_scores sheet of 04_run_singscore.xlsx."
    ), 115),
    tag_levels = "A",
    theme = theme(
      plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 9, lineheight = 1.2),
      plot.caption.position = "plot"
    )
  )
```

S11 goes to `b_reports/04_run_singscore_figures.pdf`.

```{r write-figure}
pdf(file.path(stage, "b_reports", "04_run_singscore_figures.pdf"), width = 8.27, height = 11.69)
print(figure)
invisible(dev.off())
```

## Save results

The score matrix is written twice. `set_scores.rds` is what `05_set_classification` and
`06_set_association` read: singscore values carry exact rank ties, and a round trip through Excel
changes the last bit of some, which breaks ties and moves 05's Wilcoxon and Spearman p.
`04_run_singscore.xlsx` holds the same matrix for reading, beside the collection medians and the
component check.

```{r write}
sheets <- list(
  collection_spread = collection_spread,
  structure_check = structure_check,
  set_scores = rownames_to_column(as.data.frame(scores), "set_id")
)
overview <- data.frame(
  sheet = names(sheets), rows = map_int(sheets, nrow), columns = map_int(sheets, ncol),
  description = c(
    "Median score and dispersion per collection",
    "Variance and participant share per component",
    "Set by sample score matrix"
  )
)
saveRDS(scores, file.path(stage, "c_data", "set_scores.rds"))
write_xlsx(
  c(list(overview = overview), sheets),
  file.path(stage, "c_data", "04_run_singscore.xlsx")
)
```
